name: Flowchart
what: A path of actions and decisions.
when: Use for procedures, algorithms, or branching outcomes.
how: Choose a direction such as LR or TD; connect named nodes with arrows and label decision branches.
starter:
flowchart LR
  Start --> Decide{Ready?}
  Decide -->|Yes| Done
  Decide -->|No| Wait

name: Class
what: Classes, members, and structural relationships.
when: Use for object models and interface or inheritance design.
how: Declare classes and connect them with the class relationship arrows.
starter:
classDiagram
  class Customer
  class Order
  Customer --> Order : places

name: Sequence
what: Messages exchanged in time order.
when: Use for request flows, API calls, and interactions among participants.
how: Declare participants and write arrows from sender to receiver in chronological order.
starter:
sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant API
  User->>API: Request
  API-->>User: Response

name: Entity Relationship
what: Stored entities and their cardinality.
when: Use for database schemas and data relationships.
how: Define entities and connect them with cardinality markers such as ||--o{.

name: State
what: Allowed states and transitions of one thing.
when: Use for lifecycles, protocols, or state machines.
how: Name states and connect transitions; use [*] for a start or end.
starter:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Idle
  Idle --> Active : start
  Active --> [*] : stop

name: Mindmap
what: Ideas branching from a central topic.
when: Use for brainstorming or a topic outline without a strict process order.
how: Put the root first and indent branches below their parents.
starter:
mindmap
  root((Project))
    Goals
    Risks

name: Architecture
what: Services, groups, and their deployed connections.
when: Use for infrastructure and service topology.
how: Declare services or groups with icons, then connect service sides with directional edges.
starter:
architecture-beta
  service api(server)[API]
  service db(database)[Database]
  api:R --> L:db

name: Block
what: A compact arrangement of named parts.
when: Use for a simple component layout where placement matters more than flow detail.
how: Declare a column count and place blocks in rows; quote display labels inside brackets.
starter:
block-beta
  columns 2
  a["Input"] b["Output"]

name: C4
what: Software architecture at system, container, or component level.
when: Use when the audience needs a defined architecture level and system boundaries.
how: Choose C4Context, C4Container, C4Component, C4Dynamic, or C4Deployment; declare people and systems, then Rel links.
starter:
C4Context
  Person(user, "User")
  System(app, "App")
  Rel(user, app, "Uses")

name: Cynefin Framework
what: Situations grouped by how predictable and knowable they are.
when: Use to discuss clear, complicated, complex, chaotic, or uncertain decision contexts.
how: Open each domain by name, add quoted items, and optionally show transitions between domains.
starter:
cynefin-beta
  complex
  "Unknown pattern"
  clear
  "Known procedure"

name: Event Modeling
what: A timeline of commands, events, read models, and user views.
when: Use for event-driven business behavior and information change over time.
how: Add numbered time frames with entity kinds such as ui, cmd, evt, and rmo.
starter:
eventmodeling
  tf 01 ui CartUI
  tf 02 cmd AddItem
  tf 03 evt ItemAdded

name: Gantt
what: Scheduled tasks and durations on a calendar.
when: Use for project plans with dates and dependencies.
how: Set dateFormat, add sections, then define each task with a start date and duration or end date.
starter:
gantt
  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
  section Plan
  Design :a1, 2026-01-01, 5d

name: Git
what: Commits, branches, and merges.
when: Use to explain version-control history or a branch strategy.
how: Add commit, branch, checkout, and merge statements in their intended order.
starter:
gitGraph
  commit
  branch feature
  checkout feature
  commit

name: Ishikawa
what: Possible causes feeding into a stated problem.
when: Use for root-cause discussions with grouped contributing factors.
how: Put the problem first; indent cause groups and their subcauses below it.
starter:
ishikawa-beta
  Slow response
  Code
    Expensive query
  Infrastructure
    Busy server

name: Kanban
what: Work cards arranged in workflow columns.
when: Use for current work state and task movement.
how: Declare columns, then indent cards beneath each column.
starter:
kanban
  todo[To do]
    task1[Write tests]
  done[Done]
    task2[Plan work]

name: Packet
what: Bit fields in a packet or register.
when: Use for wire formats and binary layouts.
how: Give each field a bit range or width and a quoted label.
starter:
packet
  0-7: "Version"
  8-15: "Flags"

name: Pie
what: Parts of one whole.
when: Use for a small number of nonnegative categories that sum to a meaningful whole.
how: Write quoted category labels followed by numeric values.

name: Quadrant
what: Items positioned on two qualitative axes.
when: Use for priority or comparison matrices with two dimensions.
how: Label both axes and quadrants, then place each item at normalized x,y coordinates.
starter:
quadrantChart
  x-axis Low --> High
  y-axis Low --> High
  quadrant-1 Focus
  Item: [0.7, 0.8]

name: Radar
what: Several entities compared across the same dimensions.
when: Use for a small set of comparable multivariate scores.
how: Declare axes and curves with values in the same axis order.

name: Railroad (ABNF)
what: Syntax rules written in Augmented Backus-Naur Form.
when: Use for IETF-style or other existing ABNF grammars.
how: Write rules as name = definition ; and use / for alternatives.
starter:
railroad-abnf-beta
  value = "yes" / "no" ;

name: Railroad (EBNF)
what: Syntax rules written in Extended Backus-Naur Form.
when: Use for language or configuration grammars expressed in EBNF.
how: Write rules as name = definition ; and use | for alternatives.
starter:
railroad-ebnf-beta
  value = "yes" | "no" ;

name: Railroad (IR)
what: Syntax paths built from explicit railroad primitives.
when: Use when a grammar needs a layout that ABNF, EBNF, or PEG cannot express cleanly.
how: Write rule = constructor(...) ; with terminal, sequence, choice, and related primitives.
starter:
railroad-beta
  value = choice(terminal("yes"), terminal("no")) ;

name: Railroad (PEG)
what: Syntax rules written as a Parsing Expression Grammar.
when: Use for ordered-choice parser grammars.
how: Write rules as name <- definition ; and use / for ordered alternatives.
starter:
railroad-peg-beta
  value <- "yes" / "no" ;

name: Requirement
what: Requirements and the elements that satisfy or verify them.
when: Use for traceability between formal requirements and implementation or tests.
how: Declare a requirement with id, text, risk, and verifymethod; connect an element using a typed link.
starter:
requirementDiagram
  requirement response_time {
    id: R1
    text: Reply quickly
    risk: high
    verifymethod: test
  }

name: Sankey
what: Quantified flow between stages or categories.
when: Use for resource, traffic, or cost flows where widths represent amounts.
how: Write CSV-like source,target,value rows after the declaration.
starter:
sankey-beta
  Input,Output,5

name: Timeline
what: Events arranged by date or period.
when: Use for milestones or historical progression without task durations.
how: Add a title, then period : event lines in order.
starter:
timeline
  title Project
  2026 : Start
  2027 : Finish

name: TreeView
what: A directory-like nested hierarchy.
when: Use for file trees and other indented parent-child lists.
how: Indent children beneath parents; end directory labels with /.
starter:
treeView-beta
  project/
    src/
      main.go
    README.md

name: Treemap
what: Hierarchical values shown as nested areas.
when: Use when both grouping and relative size matter.
how: Indent quoted child labels beneath parents and give leaves numeric values.
starter:
treemap-beta
  "Project"
    "Code": 70
    "Docs": 30

name: Use Case
what: Actors and goals they perform through a system.
when: Use for functional scope and user-system interactions.
how: Declare actors and use cases, optionally a system boundary, then connect them.
starter:
usecase-beta
  actor Customer("Customer")
  Checkout("Place order")
  Customer --> Checkout

name: User Journey
what: A person's steps and experience through a task.
when: Use for service or product experience, including satisfaction at each step.
how: Group tasks into sections and assign each step a score and actor.
starter:
journey
  title Signup
  section Account
    Register: 5: User
    Confirm: 3: User

name: Venn
what: Overlap among sets.
when: Use for membership and shared categories, not time or flow.
how: Declare sets before any union that names their overlap.
starter:
venn-beta
  set Frontend
  set Backend
  union Frontend,Backend["APIs"]

name: Wardley Maps
what: A value chain plotted by visibility and evolution.
when: Use for strategic discussion of user needs, dependencies, and how mature components are.
how: Place anchors or components at [visibility, evolution] coordinates, then connect dependencies.
starter:
wardley-beta
  anchor Customer [0.90, 0.95]
  component App [0.70, 0.70]
  Customer -> App

name: XY
what: Numerical values against an ordered x axis.
when: Use for trends or comparable measurements over categories or time.
how: Declare x and y axes, then add line or bar series in x-axis order.
starter:
xychart-beta
  x-axis [Jan, Feb, Mar]
  y-axis "Count" 0 --> 10
  line [2, 5, 8]

name: ZenUML
what: Sequence interactions with call-like nesting.
when: Use when nested calls, returns, or control blocks communicate behavior better than a basic sequence view.
how: Write interactions using ZenUML call or arrow syntax; its syntax differs from sequenceDiagram.
starter:
zenuml
  Alice->Bob: Request
  Bob->Alice: Response
